author: HSinghHira
tagline: Self-hosted gym and body-weight tracker with passkey login
description:
openGym is a self-hosted gym and body-weight tracker: plan routines, log workouts (supersets and cardio included), and track your weight and progress over time, all stored on your own server.

**Features**

- Weekly routine planner and guided workout logging, with supersets,
  drop-sets, rest-pause and planned warm-ups.

- Body-weight tracking with a goal line and progress charts, plus
  estimated 1RM and other stats.

- Passkey (WebAuthn) sign-in — no passwords to manage, with optional
  invite-only signup and an admin dashboard.

- Push notifications for workout-day reminders, generated on first
  run with no setup required.

- Everything is stored as plain files under /DATA/AppData/$AppID — no
  separate database container to run or back up.

- An exercise-media step downloads the exercise photo and GIF library
  (~140 MB) once on first start and shares it with the web service.


**How to use?**

1. Open openGym from the Zima OS dashboard.
2. On first visit, tap "Create profile" and register a passkey for
   your account.

3. Build your first weekly routine, then start a guided workout from
   it and log your sets as you go.

4. Add a body-weight entry and set a goal line under the Weight tab
   to start tracking progress.

5. Optional: turn on the admin dashboard, invite-only signup, or the
   AI Coach later from Settings — none of these need the container
   rebuilt.

tips.before_install:
1. This app needs two matching values before it will let anyone log
   in: RP_ID and ORIGIN, both in the api service.


2. If you are only testing this on the same computer, leave RP_ID as
   localhost and set ORIGIN to http://localhost:8435.


3. If you want to open this app from your phone or from the
   internet, you need a real domain name with HTTPS in front of it
   first.


4. In that case, set RP_ID to just the domain, like gym.example.com.

5. Set ORIGIN to the full address, like https://gym.example.com.

6. RP_ID and ORIGIN must point at the exact same address, or sign-in
   will fail.


7. Start the openGym installation.

8. The first time it starts, a helper step downloads about 140 MB of
   exercise pictures and videos. This can take a few minutes — let
   it finish before opening the app.


9. Open openGym from the Zima OS dashboard.

10. Tap "Create profile" and register a passkey to sign in. There is
    no username or password to remember.


11. Everything you do is saved under the app's data folder. Back
    that folder up regularly — it holds your whole workout history.


12. Important: if you ever move this app to a new address, every
    passkey stops working and everyone has to sign in fresh. Try to
    pick your final address before inviting other people.

title: openGym
release_note:
- Initial version

- api and web are pinned to the :latest tag rather than a specific
  version. openGym ships releases very frequently (several a day at
  times), and a pinned version tag from one day was already gone
  from the GitLab registry the next, breaking the pull. Upstream's
  own docker-compose.yml pulls :latest too, so this follows that.

- The media service also uses the floating alpine/git:latest tag,
  since it is a generic one-time download helper, not an openGym
  release, and alpine/git does not publish version tags worth
  pinning against.
